moments.name: Part 1 — Stack, split-refusal, and one price call
moments.description: Two Next.js apps on Vercel Hobby and a single serverless price-snapshot function calling an external market-data provider, plus two analytics tools that load in the browser only after consent. Bullpen as Part 1 left it.

moments.name: Part 2 — Architecture as code
moments.description: The same two Next.js apps and one serverless function as Part 1, with no new runtime node. The rules I had only stated in prompts now fail a build, and the architecture page reads the repo's own records.

metadata.planned-description: Prediction: the landing app gains an in-browser architecture explorer over this same timeline, with no new runtime nodes.

moments.name: Part 3 (planned) — Data ownership and the first split
moments.description: Prediction: the price-snapshot service splits into a Prices Service and a Market History Service, each with its own Neon Postgres database, and a proposed U.S. stock data provider (Alpha Vantage, pending written permission — see ADR-0008) appears as an external system.

moments.name: Part 4 (planned) — The order saga
moments.description: Prediction: an Orders Service, a workflow engine, and a Ledger Service turn placing a trade into a multi-step saga.

moments.name: Part 5 (planned) — Market open and the bill
moments.description: Prediction: a queue absorbs the market-open order burst, and cost/usage metadata makes the bill visible on the architecture itself.

moments.name: Part 6 (planned) — Leaderboards, leagues, and retrospective
moments.description: Prediction: a Leaderboard Service and leagues, the Part 3 stock data provider carried forward unchanged, and a retrospective comparing this prediction to what actually shipped.

metadata.title: Bullpen Architecture Timeline
metadata.description: The system's shape over time across the 'Architecting Software in 2026' blog series — one moment per part.
